body:
The split is complete and verified. `cargo check -p open-mtr-core` passes cleanly with no warnings.

## Summary

Split `core/src/openmtr/domain/newtypes.rs` (641 lines) into a `domain/newtypes/` directory:

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | 144 | Module docs + `pub use` re-exports of all 8 types + all 19 unit tests |
| `cnpj.rs` | 281 | `Cnpj`, `Cpf`, `CpfCnpj` + normalization/validation + all `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impls |
| `codigos.rs` | 100 | `CodigoIbama`, `PlacaVeiculo` + impls |
| `datas.rs` | 85 | `DataMtr`, `TimestampMs` + impls |
| `quantidade.rs` | 49 | `Quantidade` (f64 contract) + impls |

All files are ≤300 lines. The old `newtypes.rs` was deleted after the directory was in place (no E0761). `domain/mod.rs` and all downstream paths (`domain::newtypes::DataMtr`, etc.) remain unchanged — re-exports preserve the public API exactly.

Preserved verbatim:
- All doc comments moved with their items (module docs on `mod.rs`).
- All `Serialize`/`Deserialize` impls, including `DataMtr`'s `dd-MM-yyyy` (`%d-%m-%Y`) format for both `Display` and serde.
- Error strings, constructor logic, and behavior unchanged.

Note: `datas.rs` doc link `[`crate::openmtr::domain::mtr::Periodo`]` kept its fully-qualified path so rustdoc resolution still works from the new location.
